d.t: All.
An unspecified example of (something); the indefinite article.
d.e: There was a man here looking for you yesterday.

d.t: One; used before score, dozen, hundred, thousand, million, etc.
d.e: I've seen it happen a hundred times.

d.t: Used in some phrases denoting quantity, such as a few, a good many, a couple, a little, a bit, etc.
d.e: He's a bit thick, isn't he?

d.t: Used in some adverbial phrases denoting the degree or extent of an action, such as a little, a bit, a lot, etc.
d.e: The door was opened a little.

d.t: The same; one and the same. Used in phrases such as of a kind, birds of a feather, etc.
d.e: We are of a mind on matters of morals.

d.t: Any; every; used before a noun which has become modified to limit its scope.
d.e: A man who dies intestate leaves his children troubles and difficulties.

d.t: Any; used with a negative to indicate not a single one.
d.e: It was so dark that we couldn't see a thing.

d.t: Used before an adjective that modifies a noun (singular or plural) delimited by a numeral.
d.e: The lottery jackpot is worth a staggering three hundred million dollars.
